propositions: Plan review certified tickets with mutually unsatisfiable acceptance criteria across parent and children as having zero blocking findings, causing contradictions to surface only mid-implementation or at completion-verification.

No existing plan-review criterion owns the concern of whether a ticket's own acceptance criteria and Scope/Out-of-Scope declarations are jointly satisfiable; COH disclaims within-section checks, E1 covers mapping/terminology, F1 covers measurability.
A new advisory 1-TURN criterion `ac-satisfiability` in the coherence facet must detect three contradiction shapes: universal-vs-carve-out, derived-artifact closure, and snapshot cardinality.
G3's child-coverage audit cannot fire because it is handed a roster carrying only ids and titles, lacking the acceptance-criteria items needed to test whether siblings cover parent criteria.

The sibling roster is built independently in three places (pass1.py, fidelity_spot_eval.py, eval_solver.py), causing divergence between production and eval paths; a single shared `build_sibling_roster()` helper must source all three.

The roster must move from per-pairing instructions into the byte-stable system-prompt prefix, sent once rather than repeated per child pairing, and its token cost must be included in the `parent_tokens` estimate.
